atomicity.reason: One obligation, a bounded SoC error over a stated band; the parenthetical SoC definition and the reference-value sentence define terms and add no second obligation.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: the body defines state of charge, the reference value and the band; 'rated capacity' and 'calibrated bench' are standard terms.

feasibility.reason: A 3 % of rated capacity bound over 10-90 % at 25 °C is a routine target for coulomb counting with open-circuit-voltage correction, and it conflicts with nothing in the linked context or the other SoC requirements.

parent_fit.reason: Realises the parent's bench criterion point for point: a fully charged pack discharged on a calibrated bench, every reported level over the middle of the range, within a stated tolerance (3 % of rated capacity over 10-90 %).

unambiguity.reason: The core meaning is clear, but the reference is defined as a charge counted out rather than an SoC value, it is not said whether a fully charged worn pack starts at 100 % or at its faded capacity (SoC is defined against rated capacity), and the bound is stated only at 25 °C, leaving other temperatures open.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define the reference as an SoC value (starting value minus counted-out charge as a share of rated capacity) and say whether the 3 % bound applies only at 25 °C or also at other temperatures.

verifiability.reason: Tolerance, band, 25 °C condition and the bench reference are concrete, but the discharge load profile or rate and the criterion for 'fully charged' are not stated, although estimator error depends on them, so two labs could run different discharges and reach different verdicts.
verifiability.suggestion: State the bench discharge profile (e.g. a constant-current rate), the full-charge criterion and whether the pack is new or aged, so the pass/fail check is reproducible.

summary: Well-quantified accuracy bound mirroring the parent's bench criterion; held back by an unstated discharge profile and an under-specified reference basis (worn pack, temperatures other than 25 °C).
